item.title: Turn an ESP32 into a WiFi Motion Sensor: ESPectre Principles and Deployment
item.description: If you want to know whether someone is moving in a room, the two off-the-shelf options are both awkward. Cameras raise privacy problems and are off-limits in bedrooms and bathrooms. PIR sensors rely on infrared, fail behind a glass cabinet, and false-trigger on air-conditioning drafts. ESPectre takes a different angle: the room is already full of WiFi signals, and human movement disturbs them — so just read the change in the signal. It turns a ten-dollar ESP32 into a motion sensor with no camera, no microphone, and no dedicated mmWave radar; the router is the one you already own.
